heading: Sort first, check neighbors
body:
To detect overlapping meetings, **sort by start time** then check if any interval starts before the previous one ends.

If `intervals[i][0] < intervals[i-1][1]` → overlap found.

Key insight: after sorting, overlaps only appear between **consecutive** intervals.

heading: Edge case: touching endpoints
body:
Meetings like `(0,5)` and `(5,10)` do **not** conflict.

We check `start < prev_end` (strict `<`), not `<=`.

Only return `false` when intervals actually **overlap**, not just touch.

label: Crux · Python

q: What is the time complexity of this solution?
explain: Sorting the intervals takes O(n log n) time and dominates the O(n) iteration.
